Update the affected file the way we discussed, being careful to keep the

findings.note: The 'affected file' is never named anywhere in the skill, and 'the way we discussed' refers to a conversation not captured in the text.

findings.evidence: Confirm the check is no longer flaky.
findings.note: Flakiness is nondeterministic, so a single run of verification.command (python3 tests/test_ledger.py) passing once does not genuinely confirm the flake is fixed, and no repeat-run or pass-count criterion is given.

findings.evidence:
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
       subject line

       body

       Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
       EOF
findings.note: The write/blank-line/heredoc steps are self-contained and a fresh instance can execute them without any session memory or repo access.

findings.evidence: Write the commit subject and body as normal.
findings.note: The only unstated assumption is the ordinary one that you're already inside the target git repo with something staged, which is standard for any commit-writing skill and not worth spelling out.

The unquoted pattern contains an unescaped '<' and '>', which the shell parses as input/output redirection (redirecting stdin from a nonexistent file 'noreply@anthropic.com' and stdout into '.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG', truncating it) instead of as literal grep-pattern characters, so the command as written does not perform the described content check and can instead clobber the very file it's supposed to read.

findings.evidence:
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
       subject line

       body

       Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
       EOF
findings.note: The two steps give a concrete, self-contained command a fresh instance can copy verbatim without needing repo context.

findings.evidence: because the previous message has no such line
findings.note: The Verification's walkthrough silently assumes the repo's prior commit message lacked this trailer, but that assumption is never listed under Preconditions and isn't guaranteed in a repo where earlier commits already used this same skill.

findings.evidence: so this reads back your own commit
findings.note: COMMIT_EDITMSG is not cleared between commits, so if an earlier commit in this repo already carried the same trailer, grep would exit 0 even if the procedure were skipped for the current commit, making the check a false positive rather than a genuine verification.
